pseudos.text: Intuit, the tax-software company, announced a strategic pivot to pioneer new frontiers in AI-powered products, consolidating teams into strategic hubs. This organizational change involves eliminating roughly 17% of its workforce—about 3,000 full-time roles—to reshape human capital for an AI-driven future.

The chief executive communicated the decision to eliminate roles as part of a painful but necessary reinvention. To ease the journey, affected U.S. employees were offered a severance package of 16 weeks of base pay plus two weeks per year of tenure, a financial bridge for professionals facing a career crossroads.

As part of this reinvention, the company is consolidating operations, shutting down established local offices in Reno and Woodland Hills. This office closure frees the organization from legacy real estate constraints, enabling its leap into new operational models.
